rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty builder trees go (canary date palms, corals and ficus along the back fences, fan palms 1.1-6.6 m from the houses, jacarandas and a magnolia by the seating); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the grill, the adirondack chairs, the two patio sets, and the open lot corner.

trees.why: the back yard with the adirondack chair and the potted plants: a magnolia to sit under
the west back yard with the kettle grill (1.2 m off): a coral tree over the cook
the back yard with the patio set (1.7 m off): a jacaranda over the table
the north yard's patio set (1.8 m off), across the back line: the same for the neighbours
the north-west yard with the two adirondack chairs: shade for them
the open lot corner at the north-east, 20 m from the walls: an old ficus
